base_member_text: [L283-L348] (HIGH/small-direction-grid bounds) Second-order directional advection is enabled for any ntheta>1 but indexes itheta+2 at the lower boundary, which is out of bounds when ntheta=2.
audit_member_text: [L283-L348] (HIGH/small-dimension bounds) Second-order theta advection is enabled for any ntheta>1, but ntheta=2 makes the boundary stencil reference ee(:,:,3) outside the two-bin array.

adversarial.rationale: ntheta=2 is allowed by grid construction and the second-order scheme is not downgraded for two angular bins. The first boundary flux accesses bin 3 for negative ctheta, while the last boundary flux can access bin 0 for positive ctheta; the wet-cell guard does not prevent these cases.

base_member_text: [L24-L48] (MED/unbounded smoothing weight) The wave-flow smoothing factors are not capped at one, so large hydrodynamic timesteps can make the old-state coefficient negative.
audit_member_text: [L24-L47] (MED/time filtering) The temporal smoothing factor is not clamped to [0,1], so sufficiently large dt relative to wavint or cats*Trep gives a negative weight to the previous state.

adversarial.rationale: The single_dir wavint case is normally protected by wave-event scheduling and compute_dt's clipping to the next event. The remaining extrapolating filter weights require dt>cats*Trep in the other averaging path, or a caller bypassing normal timestep scheduling; positive depth alone does not protect the velocity filter.

base_member_text: [L823-L835] (HIGH/ineffective convergence failure detection) The dispersion loop can only exit with iter<=itermax, so the post-loop test always reports success even when the iteration reaches its limit without satisfying the error tolerance.
audit_member_text: [L823-L835] (HIGH/convergence reporting) iteratedispersion can never return its documented negative nonconvergence signal because the loop cannot leave with iter>itermax while the test accepts every iter<=itermax, including exhaustion at 150.

adversarial.rationale: iter starts at zero and increments only while iter<150, so exhaustion ends at 150 and the iter<=itermax test always succeeds. No caller can receive the advertised negative result from finite nonconvergent iteration.

base_member_text: [L1026-L1033, L1047-L1048] (HIGH/current-weight sign reversal) The WCI depth weight uses 1-h/hwcimax without a nonnegative clamp, so depths above hwcimax reverse rather than suppress the current contribution.
audit_member_text: [L1026-L1033,L1047-L1048] (HIGH/WCI taper) The current-interaction taper can become negative when depth exceeds hwcimax because it lacks a zero lower clamp, reversing the current contribution to intrinsic frequency and group velocity.

adversarial.rationale: The shared wave_dispersion expressions have only upper min clamps and hhlocal is not capped at hwcimax. Positive depth greater than that configurable threshold therefore makes the current multiplier negative; the later intrinsic-frequency floor does not repair wm or cgxm/cgym.

base_member_text: [L1321-L1329] (MED/unguarded physical division) Wet-cell Stokes and roller drift divide by phase speed and hstokes without enforcing positive denominators.
audit_member_text: [L1321-L1329] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Stokes and roller fluxes divide wet-cell energy by c and hstokes without lower bounds, so zero phase speed or zero hstokes yields invalid fluxes.

adversarial.rationale: The alleged zero denominators are neutralized upstream for valid model state: hh is floored at eps, hstokes is hh plus a nonnegative correction (or max(hh,hmin)), and c comes from positive intrinsic frequency/k or a 0.01 fallback. The wet mask also excludes dry velocity states.

neutralizer.quote:
if (par%oldhmin==1) then
         s%hstokes = max(s%hh,par%hmin)
      else
         gamma = s%H/s%hh
         where (gamma>1.d0)
            s%hstokes = par%deltahmin*(gamma-1.d0)*s%H+s%hh
         elsewhere
            s%hstokes = s%hh
         endwhere

adversarial.rationale: Saved work storage really persists across calls and can be wrong after changing grid size or enabling WCI mid-lifetime.
